- **Project management** — dependency resolution with universal (cross-platform) lockfiles, plus workspace support for multi-package repos

- **Tool running** — `uvx`-style ephemeral/installed CLI tools, replacing `pipx`
- **Publishing** — replaces `twine` for uploading to PyPI

It installs as a standalone binary (curl script on macOS/Linux, PowerShell on Windows) with no Rust or Python required, and also ships via pip/pipx. Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows. The README presents it as stable and production-ready, with docs at docs.astral.sh/uv.

graders.name: answers-directly
graders.evidence:
The landing page only links to the topic, so I followed through to the [Default backend](https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx/user-guide/default-backend/) page.

**What it does:** the default backend is the catch-all service that handles every URL path and host the ingress-nginx controller doesn't recognize — i.e. any request that matches no configured ingress rule gets proxied there instead of being dropped.

**Contract it must satisfy** — a service can serve as the default backend if it exposes two endpoints:

| Path | Expected response |
|---|---|
| `/healthz` | HTTP 200 (used for health checking) |
| `/` | HTTP 404 (the fallback response for unmatched traffic) |

**Customization:** the project ships a custom error pages service under `/images/custom-error-pages` in the repo, so you can replace the generic 404 with your own branded error responses rather than running the stock backend.
